macros.name: covergraphics
macros.doc: In the case you want to fill the cover or the inside of your CD with a picture, the commands \covergraphics and \insidegraphics work like \covertext and \insidetext, but they create no border (as opposed to the standard 1 cm border for text).

macros.name: fh
macros.doc: The command \fh{⟨height⟩} sets the font height to the given number of points (line spacing is not affected), while \fhb{⟨height⟩}{⟨baselineskip⟩} sets both the font height and the baseline skip (usually 6/5th of the font height will work).

macros.name: fhb
macros.doc: The command \fh{⟨height⟩} sets the font height to the given number of points (line spacing is not affected), while \fhb{⟨height⟩}{⟨baselineskip⟩} sets both the font height and the baseline skip (usually 6/5th of the font height will work).

macros.name: infofont
macros.doc: \insidefont, \spinefont, \tracklistfont, \infofont and \indexfont, that allow to change the font assigned to a part of the cover.

macros.name: insidefont
macros.doc: \insidefont, \spinefont, \tracklistfont, \infofont and \indexfont, that allow to change the font assigned to a part of the cover.

macros.name: insidegraphics
macros.doc: In the case you want to fill the cover or the inside of your CD with a picture, the commands \covergraphics and \insidegraphics work like \covertext and \insidetext, but they create no border (as opposed to the standard 1 cm border for text).

macros.name: leftinfo
macros.doc: The text contained in \leftinfo and \rightinfo is bottom-aligned just under the respective track lists.

macros.name: makeback
macros.doc: Once everything is set up, the \makecover and \makeback commands will create a cover and a back cover using the data set so far, whereas the \makeslimcover will create a slim cover.

macros.name: makecover
macros.doc: Once everything is set up, the \makecover and \makeback commands will create a cover and a back cover using the data set so far, whereas the \makeslimcover will create a slim cover.

macros.name: makelist
macros.doc: Having a database of data files is particularly useful when using the \makelist or the \makeslimlist commands, which process an entire list of CDs, printing one cover (or two back covers) per page; the crop marks are suitably aligned so to minimise the cutting effort.

macros.name: newcd
macros.doc: The \newcd command resets font and text values to its default values.

macros.name: rightinfo
macros.doc: The text contained in \leftinfo and \rightinfo is bottom-aligned just under the respective track lists.

macros.name: setindex
macros.doc: Should you need to set manually the track number, use \setindex{⟨n⟩}.

macros.name: track
macros.doc: The left and right track lists should use the \track command, which inserts a \par and an automatically numbered box with the track number.

macros.name: tracklistheight
macros.doc: The height of the track list (in millimeters) can be set with \tracklistheight, which expects a dimensionless, positive integer value.

macros.name: trackrange
macros.doc: There is also a \trackrange command that takes a parameter and adds a range indication (two numbered boxes separated by a dash).
